summary: GraviTal is a prototype that helps astronauts understand how their bodies change during long space missions. It brings muscle strength, physical capacity and vital sign trends into one accessible view, alongside a 3D body and a plan of upcoming health checks. Using synthetic data informed by NASA research, GraviTal explores how crew members could monitor their health more independently when immediate support from Earth is unavailable.
details:
GraviTal is a prototype that helps astronauts understand changes in their health during long missions, with a focus on muscle strength. It brings together an interactive 3D body, personal health trends and a mission plan, helping crew members review their condition when immediate support from Earth may be limited.

The system combines simulated wearable readings and periodic strength and aerobic tests. It compares results with each crew member’s preflight baseline and reference curves derived from NASA bed-rest studies. Its architecture separates data generation and storage, health analysis, and planning: the HealthService identifies findings, while the Planner organizes routine studies and follow-up tasks based on NASA medical standards.

The demonstration uses synthetic crew data and simulated notifications; it is not connected to real medical devices or validated for clinical use. GraviTal explores how clear, contextual information could support more autonomous health monitoring in space.
